newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols stagnant despite bond slide.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols stagnant despite bond slide.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options barely edged up even though underlying markets continued sliding lower, dealers said.
"I'm surprised how low these things are," an investment bank trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said.
Traders said there was perception that a lot of the downside risk had been priced in after this week's gradual decline in bond prices and a corresponding rise in volatilities.
Still, caution ahead of Friday's February producer price index (PPI) underpinned volatilities.
"We've got some numbers coming out tomorrow, so they're going try to keep vols pumped up a little bit until those numbers come out," said a second bank trader at CBOT.
Implied volatilities for CBOT April and June T-bond futures options were unchanged, based on the new at-the-money strike of 108, from Wednesday's closes at 9.1 and 9.5 percent respectively.
The bond market has become overwhelmingly bearish and traders said it did not even attempt a viable rebound today after its failure to sustain brief late session bounces in the past few days.
They added that that indicated the market was leaning toward the view that the Fed would raise interest rates at the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Volume was moderately good, with a lot of 1,000-lot deals going through in the CBOT pit.
An investment bank was seen selling 4,000-5,000 contracts of June 112 calls, another bank sold 2,000 legs of June 110-114 call spreads.
There were a number of medium-sized buying in April puts with strikes of 107 to 109 as traders built up gamma positions with a dowlside bias.

The April options expire in about a week on March 21 and have high gamma, which gives them quick premium acceleration against moves in bond prices. But their steep time decay kept volatilities from rising today, which meant they only benefited directional traders, not volatility traders.
Volatilities at the shorter end of the curve were somewhat firmer, but the gains were mostly limited to mid-1997 expirations.
Implied volatility for June Eurodollar futures options rose about half a point to 11.2 percent and September inched up 0.2 to 13.4, but December was unchanged at 14.7.
